pharm: Isoquinoline derivative related to papaverine; selective phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE4) inhibitor
quick: 40-80 mg three times daily (oral); 40-80 mg IM/IV (parenteral)
May be taken with or without food
Avoid unless clearly necessary; limited data
summary: Drotaverine is an isoquinoline antispasmodic structurally related to papaverine that relieves smooth muscle spasm through phosphodiesterase-4 inhibition rather than anticholinergic action. It is used for biliary and renal colic and for gastrointestinal and genitourinary smooth muscle spasm, including dysmenorrhoea. It is used in Europe and Asia and is not approved in the US or UK.
indications: Smooth muscle spasm associated with biliary colic / cholelithiasis
Gastrointestinal smooth muscle spasm (e.g. irritable bowel, spastic constipation)

dosage.n: Adjust to symptom severity; usual total 120-240 mg/day

dosage.d: 40-80 mg per dose; may repeat as needed
dosage.n: Slow IV injection with patient supine; monitor blood pressure
Switch to oral once acute spasm controlled

admin: Oral tablets may be taken with or without food, swallowed with water
Give intravenous doses slowly with the patient lying down to limit hypotension
Monitor blood pressure during and after parenteral administration
Use parenteral route for acute colic, transitioning to oral therapy
Use the lowest effective dose for symptom control
moa: Inhibits phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE4) within smooth muscle, reducing breakdown of cyclic AMP. The resulting rise in intracellular cAMP lowers intracellular calcium availability and causes relaxation of smooth muscle. The action is non-anticholinergic and is independent of autonomic innervation, allowing antispasmodic effect with fewer atropine-like adverse effects.

absolute: Severe hepatic, renal, or cardiac (heart) failure
monitor: Blood pressure, especially after intravenous dosing
Symptom relief and underlying cause of spasm

preg: Human data are limited; avoid during pregnancy unless clearly necessary and only under medical supervision, weighing benefit against uncertain risk.
lact: Insufficient data on excretion into breast milk; breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment.
renal: Not well characterised; use with caution and avoid in severe renal failure.
hepatic: Not well characterised; use with caution and avoid in severe hepatic failure as metabolism may be impaired.

major: Levodopa - drotaverine may reduce its antiparkinsonian effect
moderate: Other PDE inhibitors - additive vasodilatory effects
minor: No other clinically significant interactions well established
interactions.food: No significant food interaction; may be taken with or without food
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; possible additive hypotension and sedation
interactions.diagnostics: No significant laboratory test interference established

emergency: Severe hypotension or collapse after IV administration

monitoring: Underlying cause of the spasm (e.g. obstruction, stone)
counsel: This medicine relaxes muscle spasm and eases colicky pain
It does not treat the underlying cause; seek review if pain persists or worsens
Rise slowly after injections as dizziness or low blood pressure can occur
Avoid alcohol while taking this medicine
Report rash, swelling, fainting, or palpitations
pk: Oral within ~30-60 minutes; parenteral within minutes
Plasma peak ~45-60 minutes after oral dose
Several hours; supports three-times-daily oral dosing
pearls: Not FDA-approved; record based on EMA/SmPC/BNF sources; pending clinical review.
Not approved in the US or UK; widely used in Europe and Asia for smooth muscle spasm
Acts via PDE4 inhibition, so it lacks the anticholinergic side effects of hyoscine-type antispasmodics
Structurally related to papaverine but more potent and selective for smooth muscle
Give intravenous doses slowly with the patient supine to avoid hypotension
Relieves symptoms only; always identify and address the underlying cause of spasm
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the usual schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Overdose may cause hypotension, cardiac conduction disturbances, and CNS effects. There is no specific antidote; management is supportive and symptomatic with cardiovascular monitoring, fluid support for hypotension, and ECG monitoring. Activated charcoal may be considered if ingestion is recent.
